title: DROP INDEX
description: DROP INDEX removes an index without touching the table's data at all - queries still work afterward, they just go back to scanning the table instead of using the index. The fixtures already include an index named `idx_products_category` - drop it.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DROP INDEX
DROP INDEX <index_name> - just the index's own name, not the table it was built on.
Use DROP INDEX followed by the exact index name, idx_products_category.
expected_behavior: idx_products_category no longer exists; products itself and every row in it are completely untouched.
explanation: Dropping an index is always safe for correctness (queries fall back to a sequential scan) - the only risk is a performance regression if that index was actually being relied on, which is why removing an index in production is usually checked against real query plans first.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_indexes WHERE schemaname = 'fixtures' AND tablename = 'products' AND indexname = 'idx_products_category'
hidden_tests.label: idx_products_category is gone
